title: Cinema Europa
subtitle: A Certain Gaze architectural photography exhibition and film screening
description: The exhibition brought together work by 10 participants in the architectural photography workshop led by Marius Vasile. With Calea Moșilor Vechi as their guiding thread, the participants explored the area with heightened attention to details, shadows, structures and unexpected angles. The title A Certain Gaze borrows the spirit of the Un Certain Regard film section, proposing a curious gaze that lingers on details.

The event took place at Cinema Europa (formerly Cinema Miorița, founded in 1935) — one of the few interwar cinemas still standing in Bucharest, its Art Deco building a fragment of Calea Moșilor's more than century-long architectural history. The opening was followed by a screening of Perfect Days — a cinematic ode to a gaze that notices the beauty in seemingly ordinary things.

Photographers: Alexandra Cojocaru, Cristian Marin, Cristina Rotaru, Eugenia Dinescu, Laura Ioana Tiron, Lorena Marin, Mirela Pipoi, Carina Roșu, Simina Haiduc, Ștefana Daniela Brat. Workshop lead: Marius Vasile. Curators: Irina Antohe, Teodora Munteanu.

title: Nod Makerspace
subtitle: Comic book launch: Pe sub apă (Under the Water), part of Dâmbovița Delivery
description: The launch of the comic book Pe sub apă (Under the Water) by Maria Mălcică took place as part of the Dâmbovița Delivery – Regie event. The project proposed a fresh look at the Dâmbovița river through a fantastical narrative grounded in real scientific data.

The plants, birds and fish illustrated in the album reflect species adapted to the urban environment of the Dâmbovița corridor. The specialist research was carried out with the support of students and teaching staff from the Faculty of Biology in Bucharest. The project supported Nod Makerspace's efforts to revitalise the river and open it up to the community.

title: GAEP Gallery
subtitle: Guided architecture tour of the Floreasca neighbourhood
description: The tour, guided by architectural historian Andrei Răzvan Voinea (Studio Zona), looked at the urban evolution of the Floreasca neighbourhood, tracing its transition from a semi-rural area on the city's edge to well-structured residential ensembles.

The route began at GAEP Gallery, housed on the ground floor of a 1950s apartment block, where participants visited the exhibition Wild Metaphysics, then continued through the historic Cornescu and Drumul la Tei housing plots, originally developed by the Municipal Society for Affordable Housing. Along the way, the tour examined the shift from the interwar housing model to the first low-rise collective housing ensembles of the 1950s, focusing on how these stages of urban development managed to preserve the neighbourhood's human scale.

title: NON art space
subtitle: Artist Talk: Art in the domestic space
description: The talk traced the path of art in the domestic space, from the first cabinets of curiosities (Wunderkammern) to contemporary independent and alternative practices, looking at how spatial settings shape artistic production, display and the relationship with the public.

The meeting was opened by Raluca Bujor, philosophy teacher and researcher, with a conceptual introduction on the evolution of exhibition spaces. It was followed by contributions from artist and journalist Nicoleta Moise, on the relationship between the intimacy of a home studio and field research; from artist and researcher Jean-Lorin Sterian (founder of Homefest), who brought an anthropological view of domestic performativity and of the living room turned into a stage; and from architect Dimitrie Grigorescu (founder of NON artspace), who described the experience of setting up a hybrid space for living and exhibiting, open to the community.

title: Museum of Maps and Old Books
subtitle: 1:1 architectural photography exhibition
description: The 1:1 exhibition invites you to discover the details that caught the eye of those who walked the streets of Dorobanți. The exhibition sits at the intersection of two ways of perceiving space: the abstract (top-down) and the personal (bottom-up). Through photography, the mapped area loses its theoretical character and becomes a lived place, brought to life through direct exploration and through the intersecting gazes of several observers.

The selection of images is the result of a workshop led by architect and photographer Marius Vasile, in which ten participants set out on a tour of the Capitale-Dorobanți neighbourhood. The event took place at the National Museum of Maps and Old Books.

Photographers: Alexandra Cojocaru, Cristian Marin, Cristina Rotaru, Eugenia Dinescu, Laura Ioana Tiron, Lorena Marin, Mirela Pipoi, Carina Roșu, Simina Haiduc, Ștefana Daniela Brat. Project team — Workshop lead: Marius Vasile; Curators: Irina Antohe, Teodora Munteanu; Museum consultant: Ioana Marinescu (museum curator).

title: Reading circle: Space. Body. City
subtitle: Theoretical meetings on space and architecture at the CdRF Library
description: This series of meetings offered a theoretical reflection on space and architecture, structured over five monthly sessions hosted by the Centre for Photographic Resources. Starting from foundational studies and concepts, the discussions aimed at a temporary defamiliarisation from the everyday built environment and explored themes such as the act of building, domestic space, the political dimension of public space, and heterotopias.

Programme and reading list: 16 May — Socrates' Ancestor, Indra Kagis McEwen (on the act of building); 19 June — The Poetics of Space, Gaston Bachelard (on domestic space and intimacy); 17 July — Real Utopias. The Utopian Body, Michel Foucault (on space, the human body and heterotopias); 28 August — Life Between Buildings. Using Public Space, Jan Gehl (on the use of public space and human scale); 18 September — Common Space. The City as Commons, Stavros Stavrides (on urban configurations and the right to the city).
The books used over the five meetings were made available at the CdRF Library with the support of Bookster and remain available for public consultation. Moderator: Raluca Bujor.

title: Architectural photography workshop
subtitle: Workshop led by architect and photographer Marius Vasile
description: The workshop led by architect and photographer Marius Vasile proposed exploring Bucharest's built space as a tool for understanding and analysing the urban environment. Structured over three days, the module combined a theoretical and practical session at MATER Library (Nod Makerspace) with two field sessions.

8 May — Introductory session on architectural photography technique, framing, working with natural light and taking a critical approach to built heritage. 9 May — Guided photo tour of the Dorobanți neighbourhood, documenting the stylistic diversity of an area shaped in the early 20th century by the Filipescu land subdivision and still evolving through contemporary architectural interventions. 10 May — Guided photo tour along Calea Moșilor Vechi, exploring a historic axis of the city marked by layered styles, urban fragmentation and contemporary interventions.
The workshop served as a working stage and a way of gathering visual material for the Filtru Cultural project's later exhibitions. Workshop lead: Marius Vasile.

title: Masca Theatre
subtitle: Photography/photo-collage exhibition and talk about the Militari neighbourhood
description: The photography exhibition explored the Militari neighbourhood as a place of contrasts: socialist architecture, chaotic urban development, makeshift solutions, community resistance, an industrial platform, commercial spaces, housing.

Photographers: Vanessa Voicu, Roxana Babiciu, Robert Zamfir, Mihai Rotaru, Marius Raiu, Mălina Moncea, Louis Jamal, Laura Iordache, Korosy Armin Endre, Elena Dobrescu, Daniel Tudor, Dana Iordan, Crina Stanciu, Anne Leonte, Alexandru Hornea.

The exhibition opening featured a discussion about the “living history” of the Militari neighbourhood, between identity, memory and emotional value. The discussion was part of the La Liber series organised by Masca Theatre and was moderated by Raluca Bujor, philosophy teacher and member of the Filtru Cultural București team, together with Răzvan Voinea & Elena Trifan — members of Politeia — and Alina Crăiță & Vladimir Purdel — Masca actors.

Among other things, we learned why the Militari neighbourhood had no park for so long, the story of Lacul Morii (the Mill Lake), what became of the area's former industrial zones, and how small gestures of resistance can bring about change.

title: Paper Traffic
subtitle: Comic book launch and community dinner
description: To learn more about the Obor area as a cultural horizon, we collaborated with Paper Traffic, located right on the terrace of the old market hall (1936–1950). A publishing house, gallery, barbershop and hotspot for backgammon championships, the small space run by Paper Traffic blends harmoniously into the orderly chaos of the food market.

The event opened with the launch of a comic book about the Obor Market area – HAI PE-AICI (This Way), by Maria Mălcică. The author explored the neighbourhood through the eyes of two friends, flâneurs rather than mere shoppers.
“From the very beginning, I wanted to invent as little as possible for this comic book. I have never lived in Obor, so I felt that a recording would be more fitting than a description.

But the rigorously documentary approach I initially wanted died in its infancy when, after a week of failed attempts to find an ‘insider’ to talk to, a kind vendor took pity on me and told me straight: ‘Good luck with your project, but you'll have a hard time finding someone to sit and chat with you. The time I spend talking to you is time I'm not selling. And me, at the end of the day, all I want is to get to my car and go home.’ So I took the advice and changed course. That ‘hard time’, which I would normally have taken as a challenge, couldn't be overcome in the time I had to spend in Obor. In fact, I worked on this comic book from four different cities and thought about it in at least eight. Each time, the first step was to transport myself to Obor one way or another, which was easier from Bucharest and harder from other cities, villages, countries. When my photos and notes (inevitably) proved insufficient, my browser filled up with tabs for ‘obor vlog’, ‘obor park’, ‘google maps obor’, ‘obor market halls’, ‘mici obor’ and so on.

Since the people remained, from a certain point on, inaccessible to me – apart from conversations overheard in passing – I was guided instead by objects, structures, spaces. In a place like this, commercial par excellence, it would have been easy for the mercantile dimension to smother all the others. That is how the protagonists came about: bounded flâneurs rather than consumers. And their wandering among vegetables, detergents, clothes and jars became all the more labyrinthine without a shopping list.” (Foreword by Maria Mălcică).

The launch was rounded off by a community dinner, which sparked conversations about the changes Obor Market and other Bucharest markets have gone through, the possibility of gentrification, and the place of culture in a deeply commercial space.

title: Ioan Hanciu House
subtitle: Architectural treasure hunt
description: Participants received a map with clues and were invited to discover emblematic details of the modernist style, typical of the houses built between 1933 and 1949 under the direction of architects Ioan Hanciu and Nicolae Aprihăneanu.

The features they searched for included original ironwork, geometric balconies, stained glass, Art Deco details and other traces of the interwar housing plots. The activity aimed to familiarise participants with the vocabulary of modernist architecture and with Bucharest's history from the perspective of its architectural evolution.
!Guided tour of the Vatra Luminoasă neighbourhood and the Ioan Hanciu House
Conceived in the interwar period as a garden city, the neighbourhood was built by Casa Construcțiilor between 1933 and 1949, to plans by architects Ioan Hanciu and Nicolae Aprihăneanu.

Participants followed a walking route that included examples of modernist popular housing with Art Deco elements, private gardens and community amenities. The tour highlighted the typological diversity and architectural coherence of the neighbourhood, as well as the story behind these buildings designed for clerks and workers. The tour also included a stop at a house recently restored by Vinklu and Blanc Architecture, as an example of good practice in architecture.

The tour was rounded off with a visit to the Hanciu House, opened to the public every year by the architect's great-grandson, Jérémy Vercken. Visitors could see not only the architect's house but also the temporary exhibition “Silent Blueprints” by artist Albert Kaan.

title: The “Tudor Arghezi” Memorial House
subtitle: Cultural treasure hunt for children with Ana Rubeli
description: Participants were invited to explore the writer's house and garden, guided by a series of riddles that led them to objects representative of Tudor Arghezi's world. The activity gave them the chance to discover, interactively, details of the poet's life and work, as well as the history of the place where he lived and wrote, together with his family, from 1930 until the end of his life.

The clues included “Zdreanță's kennel”, which invited children to find the spot where the famous dog from Arghezi's poem used to rest; “The poet's cane”, a symbol of his presence in the house; and “The glasses”, the object through which the author looked at the world and turned it into verse.

The exploration involved careful observation, photography or drawing. At the end, the children presented their findings and were rewarded with a surprise. The activity encouraged direct interaction with cultural heritage and brought to the fore the story of the place where Tudor Arghezi lived and wrote, in a way that was accessible and memorable for young audiences.

title: Casa Scânteii. A Landscape in Transformation
subtitle: Lecture by architect Irina Tulbure
description: After getting an inside view from two of the artists working at Atelierele Scânteia, we turned our attention to the exterior of this city landmark. We had the pleasure of welcoming architect Irina Tulbure, who spoke to us about the many rewritings of the area around the House of the Free Press, from the Luna Bucureștilor amusement park, the Romexpo exhibition complex and the former EREN Pavilion to the Jiului neighbourhood.

“The story of Casa Scânteii began under the sign of change and of a clear intention to create a model that would be mandatory to follow in the rewriting of the Romanian urban landscape after the Second World War. That is not quite what happened. For a while, the city of tall buildings, with towers, columns and ornaments, was no longer the aim of urban planning projects. And so a new stage followed in the reshaping of the space around Casa Scânteii: exhibitions, modern architecture, hotels, greenery, boldness and yet another rewritten landscape. The buildings rising today near Casa Scânteii also occupy, with their own stories, that same place, which is becoming ever more constrained and densely built.” (Irina Tulbure)

title: On the Threshold: Artistic Practices in Dialogue with Public Space
subtitle: Round table talk with Cristina Vasilescu and Raluca Bujor
description: How does Suprainfinit Gallery manage to keep up a dialogue with passers-by, neighbours and public space, in a residential neighbourhood with a significant historical weight? How can artistic practices encourage residents to claim public space?

In the play of boundaries that every urban space involves, through the way they are invested with meaning and claimed, thresholds can give rise to practices through which a community (ephemeral or stable) reclaims its “right to the city”, that is, manages to turn public space into common space (S. Stavrides, 2023). But what, in the end, does “common space” mean, and what role can “threshold spaces” play in its emergence?

These questions were the starting point for the discussion at this Filtru Cultural București event, hosted by Suprainfinit Gallery. Around an imaginary round table, we explored the relationship between art and public space with Cristina Vasilescu, the gallery's curator, and Raluca Bujor, PhD in Philosophy, high school teacher and researcher.

title: Popa Tatu & Friends
subtitle: Street photography exhibition
description: Together with the Centre for Photographic Resources, we put together a group exhibition of photographs selected through an open call. The aim was to explore the urban context around CdRF and capture the atmosphere of the area through the lens. Here are some of the streets that were explored: Str. Mircea Vulcănescu, Str. Crișana, Str. Transilvaniei, Str. Horațiu, Str. Tomișana, Str. General H. M. Berthelot, Str. Iulia Hașdeu.

The exhibition featured work by the following photographers: Alex Canjea, Alexandru Hornea, Andreea Bușuioc, Andu Ghizdavet, Cătălin Mihai, Cristina Popa, Daniel Tudor, Duma Gabriel, Emma Brahas, Grecu Daniel, Iulia Ioana Dima, Cristian Juravle, Marius Raiu, Cezar Niculescu, Roxana Babiciu, Ruxandra Nanu, Ștefania Crăciun, Teodor Georgescu, Vanessa Alexandra Voicu, Vlad Mihai.
